title: Influence of intraperitoneal instillation of local anaesthetics in bariatric surgery on pain optimisation, reduction of drug consumption, minimisation of side effects and reduction of hospital length of stay
summary:
The current German guideline for post-surgical pain management (2021) recommends using a local anesthetic directly inside the abdominal cavity for minimally invasive stomach surgeries. In our study, we aim to investigate how well this method works specifically for weight-loss surgeries (bariatric procedures).  Our goal is to determine whether administering the local anesthetic Ropivacaine 0.2% directly into the abdominal cavity after surgery helps to improve pain control, reduce the need for pain medication,  minimize side effects such as nausea and vomiting caused by strong painkillers (opioids), and shorten the length of hospital stay.
These findings could help improve pain management after bariatric surgeries in the future.

interventions.name: Intraperitoneal instillation of Ropivacaine (0.2%, 100 ml) at the beginning of the operation.
Intraperitoneal instillation of NaCl solution (0.9%, 100 ml) at the beginning of the operation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Body Mass Index (BMI) > 40 or BMI > 35 with at least one comorbidity (e.g., diabetes mellitus, osteoarthritis, hypertension, and/or obstructive sleep apnea).
Approval for surgery after a multidisciplinary bariatric evaluation
Exclusion criteria:
Psychological unfitness after screening.
American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class 4 or higher.
Previous bariatric or stomach surgery.
Age < 18 or > 65 years.
Allergy to Ropivacaine.
